items.title: Jimmy Wormworth interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 6, 2002
items.q: oh Roy Haynes of course — and I can’t help but think that George Lawrence Stone’s teaching and his book in particular influenced those guys.

ctx.x: And I don’t think I remember practicing at all. I can remember one of my aunts threatening me to practice, so I must have practiced some, but I know I went through his whole course in about 2-1/2 years, from 10 to about 12-1/2, and it included a few books. It started out with a book he had written, a beginner’s book that taught you four strokes, and then taught you how to put the strokes together to make up the 26 rudiments, and then he used the Haskell Harr books which were pretty well known in that time period,…
When you were out on the road, let’s see this would have been the 50s?
